messages:
carla: heads-up: rolling a canary for aurora-11b-int4-hybrid tonight. seeing reproducible KV churn + transient OOMs during warmup when a mix of short chats and one long summarize (≈3k tokens) hit the same host. also a small ROUGE dip (~0.5) on long-doc summarization tests. dropping notes here. :mag:

noah: please paste the runner config and a short repro. any slab/gpu traces?

carla: runner (trimmed):

```
model: aurora-11b-int4-hybrid
batch_target: auto
max_new_tokens: 256
kv_prefetch: smart
kv_prefetch_window: 0
kv_hybrid_mode: auto-fp16-on-long-gen
slot_compactor_interval: 60s
soft_reserve: 0.10
```

repro: cold cluster, spin 12 short chats (~100-200 tokens) then issue one long summarize (~3000 tokens). one host drops to <3% free slots, compactor reclaims ~600MiB and host recovers; occasionally a transient OOM is reported.

maya: allocator excerpt pasted from node logs: 

```
[2026-03-24T02:11:12Z] gpu_alloc fail 1.08GiB
[2026-03-24T02:11:13Z] kv_live_bytes=4.0GiB
[2026-03-24T02:11:14Z] free_slots_frac=0.028
[2026-03-24T02:11:17Z] compactor reclaimed=620MiB
```

trent: pattern looks like: smart prefetch (default) is pulling too much for long-gen cases and hybrid_kv is kicking in late, so there's a transient memory cliff. two ideas we've used before: 1) reduce default max_new_tokens for this variant to 48 or 64 (long tails blow up KV), 2) make hybrid_kv_mode proactive: pre-allocate fp16 KV when predicted_gen_len > 512 so we avoid late conversion allocation spikes.

noah: curious about the ROUGE drop. is that only for >1k token summaries?

carla: yes, degraded mostly on summaries >800 tokens; short summaries are within noise of FP32 baseline. hypothesis: quantization noise accumulates in KV keys/values and positional drift impacts final decoding probability mass for long sequences. need a targeted eval with FP32 vs INT4-KV hybrids to isolate.

maya: propose a conservative canary plan (rollback-safe):
- set max_new_tokens default = 64 for aurora-11b-int4-hybrid
- set kv_prefetch_window = 256 (limit eager prefetch)
- enable hybrid_kv_proactive_threshold = 512 (allocate fp16-KV when expected gen length > 512)
- set batch_pacing_ms = 45 on canary hosts
- reduce slot_compactor_interval = 25s on canary hosts
- warmup_soft_reserve = 0.14
- enable per-request trace tagging for sampled long-gen flows

carla: I'll open PR with the config changes and a canary rollout at 5% of Dedicated pool. target is ~2k requests over 6 hours or 4 hours + 1k long-gen samples.

trent: operational targets for canary: p95 token latency < 155ms, post-warmup memory cushion >= 512MiB, ROUGE >= baseline - 0.6. if ROUGE delta > 0.6 -> immediate rollback and per-layer activation capture.

noah: also add a short experiment: perform per-layer FP32 vs INT4 activation L2 snapshots on 50 long examples to see which layers accumulate most error. if it's concentrated in the early attention layers, we may hot-swap those layers to fp16 KV permanently.

maya: small scheduler tweak: introduce inter-microbatch spacing of 30ms for warmup hosts to smooth allocation spikes. cost: small p95 bump. benefit: fewer transient OOMs in prior tests.

carla: minimal curl to hit the canary (replace TOKEN):

```
curl -sS -X POST https://dedicated-canary.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Model: aurora-11b-int4-hybrid" \ 
  -d '{"input":"<long summarization prompt>","max_new_tokens":64}'
```

qa-bot: :lab_coat: scheduled eval harness: 160 long-doc summaries + 300 short chats. capturing per-token latencies, per-layer L2, and top-k logprob diffs. job_id=eval/2026-03-24-aurora-01.

trent: alerting rules to wire: memory_cushion < 256MiB -> rollback, ROUGE delta > 0.6 -> rollback, p95 token latency > 220ms -> scale-down canary and investigate.

carla: PR #2154 opened (config + scheduling tweak + telemetry). kicking off canary now. will post aggregated metrics when eval job finishes.

deploy-bot: :robot_face: canary policy applied  aurora-11b-int4-hybrid -> 5% Dedicated canary. PR: #2154 opened by carla.

noah: thanks  i'll hook the eval outputs to compare FP32 baseline vs canary and run the per-layer diff. ping me when job posts results.

carla: will do. if we see ROUGE drift concentrated in a small set of layers we'll try a targeted per-layer fp16 KV mapping next (hotfix path). updating this thread as results come in. :rocket:
